title: Defining Receiving Preferences
titles: Enabling GS1 Scan On Receiving Preferences
breadcrumbs: Enabling GS1 Scan On Receiving Preferences

A receiving preference record allows you to manage how a user or group 
 of users will process receipts. The *Default record should accommodate 
 the majority of employees. Create specific preference records for employees 
 with unique processing needs.
Verify Item Unit of Measure Checkbox
Provide a record name in the Preference Name Field, and provide a description.

Use the Default 
 Receiving Dock Field to identify where the employee typically receives 
 product. When this product is putaway via an RF, the value will appear 
 in the From Loc Field.

Use the Default 
 Inventory Status Field to define the status all product will be 
 assigned during check in. Generally, you should select the value Available. 
 If you are creating this record for someone processing returns, you may 
 want to define a hold or damaged status here.

Use the Work 
Type Field to associate this record with a work type. Generally, 
 you should select the value Receiving. The system generates labor management 
 records based on work type. If you want to review history records for 
 receiving, you will need to define a work type here.

Use the Work 
 Team Field to associate this record with a work team. Members on 
 a work team share the following characteristics: same work zones, equipment 
 types and work profiles.

Use the Allow 
 Over Receiving Checkbox if this employee can receive more product 
 than is identified in the Original Total Quantity Field on the receipt 
 line. If the employee does over receive, the system will not display 
 any warning message or require any overrides on an RF device.

Use the Create 
 Putaway Work Checkbox if you want the system to generate work instructions 
 for the located containers. If you select this checkbox, the system will 
 call work creation and generate putaway instructions as soon as the container 
 is located. The system releases the work automatically. If you don't select 
 this checkbox, the system will not create work for what's located. Instead, 
 it will automatically locate the container and put its quantity as On 
 Hand at the destination location(s). Someone will need to ensure that 
 the product is physically delivered to that location(s).

Use the Execute 
 Group Putaway Checkbox to indicate that you want users (assigned 
 to this preference) to be eligible to process group putaways when locating 
 product. When these users locate received items, each item will be assigned 
 to one "putaway group," according to the group's settings (as 
 defined on the Putaway Group Window).

Use the Cross Dock Immediate Needs Checkbox to indicate that the system will attempt to locate product to the shipping dock location when fulfilling an immediate needs request. However, if this is not selected, then the system will attempt to locate only to put-to-store or immediate needs locations.

Use the License Plate 
 Assignment Method Buttons to identify if the user will assign 
 or verify license plate IDs.

• If you select system, the 
 user never assigns a license plate ID; the system always assigns it. This 
 applies to receipt containers generated during check in and manually created 
 containers used to nest checked in product.

• If you select manual, the 
 user will assign the license plate ID as long as you are not checking in product 
 to be grouped together for locating. In other words, the user will assign 
 the license plate ID to manually created containers used to nest checked in 
 product. The user will also assign the license plate ID during check in if 
 the Group During Check In Checkbox is not selected for this item. This 
 checkbox is on the Storage Template Window. If it's selected, the checked 
 in product will be located to one location, regardless of how much there 
 is. In this case, the system will require the user to verify that he/she 
 accepts the license plate ID that the system assigned.

Use the Initiation 
 Method (Workflow) Field to indicate the initiation workflow that you want the user to use during the RF receiving process. Included in each workflow are the separate activities that will occur during the pre-execution stage of RF receiving. Examples of these activities are the "initiation" field that the system will prompt for at the beginning of RF receiving (such as receipt ID, item, etc), whether QC inspection is active, or whether GS1 processing is to be used. See the
for more detailed information on how to use workflow with RF receiving.
Note that this field includes only the workflows that have been defined in the Initiation Workflow Window.
For warehouse mobile - The following SRC screen flow can be set for the following
- Receiving 30 - Receiving preference initiation method is Header-Item, then this will be set as SRC identifier
- Receiving via License Plate (50) - Receiving preference for initiation method is License Plate.
- Null - if the receiving preference is other than Header item or license-initiated method
When system is upgraded, then these existing receiving preferences will be retained in the warehouse mobile menu.
When receiving preference is saved the warehouse mobile menu will be automatically created for that preference.

Use the Application Identifier Template Field to determine how GS1 barcodes will be parsed by SCALE during 
 RF receipt check in. Note that this field is only used in the system if GS1 processing is in your initiation workflow.

Select the Nest 
 During Check In Checkbox to indicate that you want to nest container(s) 
 on a receipt into one container. At the end of the check in process, the 
 system will display a screen where you will enter a container ID and the 
 container type.  The 
 system then will nest the container(s) that you checked in during that 
 “session” into the new container. Note that you can configure security 
 for this process to skip nesting (see the "RF Receiving Container 
 Nesting" value in the Security Window).

Select the Process 
 Immediate Needs Checkbox to indicate that you want the system to 
 check to see if the item(s) that you are currently checking in has an 
 existing immediate needs request associated with it. If this checkbox 
 is checked, the system will process the immediate need for this item, 
 if one exists.

Use the Execution 
 Method Field to indicate how you want the system to process the 
 items you are receiving in to the warehouse:

• Check In: In this method, 
 the system will check in only the container(s) that you entered. The system 
 will perform this action using a batch process.

• Check In and Locate: In 
 this method, the system will check in and locate the container(s) that 
 you enter, using the appropriate locating rule. The system will perform 
 this action using a batch process. With this method, the system will also 
 create work for the putaway actions (if the Create Putaway Work for this 
 window is checked) generated from the locating process.

• Check In and Locate (Immediate): 
 In this method, the system will check in and locate the container(s) that 
 you enter, using the appropriate locating rule. The system will perform 
 this action immediately after the user presses OK, not using a batch process. 
 With this method, the system will also create work for the putaway actions 
 (if the Create Putaway Work for this window is checked) generated from 
 the locating process. Also, to create putaway groups by RF, you must choose 
 this execution method.

• Quick Receive-User: In this 
 method, the system will check in and locate the container(s) that you 
 enter, and provide a separate screens for each entity checked in that 
 allows the user to indicate where they want the container to be putaway. 
 The system does not create putaway work using this method.

• Quick Receive-System: In 
 this method, the system will check in the container(s) that you enter, 
 and attempt to locate each according to the appropriate locating rule. 
 The system will display a screen for each container displaying either 
 the location it has chosen to locate to, or asking the user to provide 
 a location if none could be found. The system does not create putaway 
 work using this method.

Use the Bypass Location Capacity Validation Checkbox to indicate that the system will suppress the following validations (any other validations will remain to be enforced): dimensions (length, width, height, weight), volume, and item location capacity.
This setting has the following behavior depending on which quick receiving execution method is used:
: The validations mentioned above will always be bypassed.
: The validations mentioned above will be bypassed only if the user is overriding the system-selected location.

Use the Override System Selected Location Checkbox to indicate if the user should be able to enter an alternate putaway location (different than the system-selected location) during license plate check in (when using the Quick Receive-System execution method). Note that you cannot use this setting when using the Quick Receive-User execution method.

Use the Container 
 Locating Method Field to identify how product will be located 
 in the warehouse. If you select the value Parent, the system will locate 
 the largest container value. For example, if Container B is a pallet and holds 10 nested cases, 
 the system will locate Container B. The 10 nested containers are moved 
 with Container B; they cannot be located to separate locations. Conversely, 
 if you select the value Child, the system will locate the lowest container 
 level. Using the example above, the system would locate the 10 cases; 
 it would not attempt to locate the entire pallet to a location. The system 
 would select the locations based on the UM dimensions defined for a case. Note that when you select to locate the Child level, the system 
 does not consider individual units to be containers. In other words, it 
 would not try to break open a container and locate its contents.
Locate By Parent Container Note: Locating by parent will only locate to multi-item locations, regardless of whether the child containers under that parent have multiple items or not.

Use the Disposition Code Required Checkbox to indicate that the user needs to scan in a disposition code that the 

system will associate with each item checked in. A disposition code indicates if an item is in good condition, is 

damaged, etc. These are helpful when processing returns.

Use the Reason Code Required Checkbox to have the system force the user to enter a reason code when checking in items. 

Note that this setting is only available when the Disposition Code Required checkbox is selected. Reason codes can be 

configured in the Quality History Reason Codes Window (set the process to Receiving).

Use the Single Unit Scan Checkbox to  perform a rapid scanning of individual items for receipt check in. When this configuration is set, you can perform a receipt check in of single unit of item without the system displaying the partial check in screen. When a single unit is scanned, then system will  check in for one quantity in the base unit of measurement and then update the receipt header, detail quantity and adjust the inventory at receiving dock locations.  Note: This option will be disabled if any one of the options are selected/active in the receiving preference - Allow over receiving, License plate assignment method is set to 'Manual', Disposition code required, QC inspection selected, Verify item dimension and Verify item unit of measure.

Use the QC Inspection Active Checkbox to that you want the system to check every item you check in to see if 

it is eligible for the quality control process.

Use the Verify Item Dimensions Checkbox to determine if the system will check item dimensions when checking in items. If 

any item does not have dimension(s), the user can choose whether the check in should continue or not:- If this checkbox 

is selected, the system will display a message warning the user that all the dimensions are not defined. The user then 

will be able to continue or cancel the check in, knowing that all the dimensions are not defined. Choose "Yes" 
 to continue with the check in, or "No" to cancel.- If the checkbox is not selected, the system will not check to see 

if an item has dimensions when performing a check in.

Use the Verify 
 Item Unit of Measure Checkbox to determine if the user is required to confirm that a receipt 
 has the same quantity per container as the system expects:

- If this checkbox is selected, 
 the system will display a verification window each time this user checks 
 in a container. This verification window displays the unit of measure 
 amounts that are defined on the storage template record for the item or 
 item class (or the

record). The user can either attest that these 
 values are correct or change them. Any changes made apply only containers 
 on this receipt.

- If this 
 checkbox is not selected, the system will not ask the user to verify the container's quantity.
Note that this setting also applies when creating pre-check in receipt containers.

The Authorized Users Tab is  used to authorize users for the preference record. A user can be authorized to one to many receiving preferences. On creating a new receiving preference, all users will be automatically authorized to the new preference.  Using the List option, the user authorization can be restricted. Only receiving preferences for the authorized user will be available from the Receipt workbench and RF Receiving screens.

 Method (Workflow) Field to indicate the initiation workflow that you want the user to use during the RF receiving process. Included in each workflow are the separate activities that will occur during the pre-execution stage of RF receiving. Examples of these activities are the "initiation" field that the system will prompt for at the beginning of RF receiving (such as receipt ID, item, etc), whether QC inspection is active, or whether GS1 processing is to be used. See the SCALE SDK for more detailed information on how to use workflow with RF receiving.

Note that this field includes only the workflows that have been defined in the Initiation Workflow Window.



For warehouse mobile - The following SRC screen flow can be set for the following

- Receiving 30 - Receiving preference initiation method is Header-Item, then this will be set as SRC identifier

- Receiving via License Plate (50) - Receiving preference for initiation method is License Plate.

- Null - if the receiving preference is other than Header item or license-initiated method



Note:

 When system is upgraded, then these existing receiving preferences will be retained in the warehouse mobile menu.

 When receiving preference is saved the warehouse mobile menu will be automatically created for that preference.







            
Use the Application Identifier Template Field to determine how GS1 barcodes will be parsed by SCALE during 
 RF receipt check in. Note that this field is only used in the system if GS1 processing is in your initiation workflow.





            
Select the Nest 
 During Check In Checkbox to indicate that you want to nest container(s) 
 on a receipt into one container. At the end of the check in process, the 
 system will display a screen where you will enter a container ID and the 
 container type.  The 
 system then will nest the container(s) that you checked in during that 
 “session” into the new container. Note that you can configure security 
 for this process to skip nesting (see the "RF Receiving Container 
 Nesting" value in the Security Window).





            
Select the Process 
 Immediate Needs Checkbox to indicate that you want the system to 
 check to see if the item(s) that you are currently checking in has an 
 existing immediate needs request associated with it. If this checkbox 
 is checked, the system will process the immediate need for this item, 
 if one exists.





            
Use the Execution 
 Method Field to indicate how you want the system to process the 
 items you are receiving in to the warehouse:



• Check In: In this method, 
 the system will check in only the container(s) that you entered. The system 
 will perform this action using a batch process.



• Check In and Locate: In 
 this method, the system will check in and locate the container(s) that 
 you enter, using the appropriate locating rule. The system will perform 
 this action using a batch process. With this method, the system will also 
 create work for the putaway actions (if the Create Putaway Work for this 
 window is checked) generated from the locating process.



• Check In and Locate (Immediate): 
 In this method, the system will check in and locate the container(s) that 
 you enter, using the appropriate locating rule. The system will perform 
 this action immediately after the user presses OK, not using a batch process. 
 With this method, the system will also create work for the putaway actions 
 (if the Create Putaway Work for this window is checked) generated from 
 the locating process. Also, to create putaway groups by RF, you must choose 
 this execution method.



• Quick Receive-User: In this 
 method, the system will check in and locate the container(s) that you 
 enter, and provide a separate screens for each entity checked in that 
 allows the user to indicate where they want the container to be putaway. 
 The system does not create putaway work using this method.



• Quick Receive-System: In 
 this method, the system will check in the container(s) that you enter, 
 and attempt to locate each according to the appropriate locating rule. 
 The system will display a screen for each container displaying either 
 the location it has chosen to locate to, or asking the user to provide 
 a location if none could be found. The system does not create putaway 
 work using this method.





            
Use the Bypass Location Capacity Validation Checkbox to indicate that the system will suppress the following validations (any other validations will remain to be enforced): dimensions (length, width, height, weight), volume, and item location capacity.



This setting has the following behavior depending on which quick receiving execution method is used:



• Quick Receive-User: The validations mentioned above will always be bypassed.



• Quick Receive-System: The validations mentioned above will be bypassed only if the user is overriding the system-selected location.





            
Use the Override System Selected Location Checkbox to indicate if the user should be able to enter an alternate putaway location (different than the system-selected location) during license plate check in (when using the Quick Receive-System execution method). Note that you cannot use this setting when using the Quick Receive-User execution method.



        

        
 

        
Using the Workbench Tab

        

            
Use the Container 
 Locating Method Field to identify how product will be located 
 in the warehouse. If you select the value Parent, the system will locate 
 the largest container value. For example, if Container B is a pallet and holds 10 nested cases, 
 the system will locate Container B. The 10 nested containers are moved 
 with Container B; they cannot be located to separate locations. Conversely, 
 if you select the value Child, the system will locate the lowest container 
 level. Using the example above, the system would locate the 10 cases; 
 it would not attempt to locate the entire pallet to a location. The system 
 would select the locations based on the UM dimensions defined for a case. Note that when you select to locate the Child level, the system 
 does not consider individual units to be containers. In other words, it 
 would not try to break open a container and locate its contents.



Locate By Parent Container Note: Locating by parent will only locate to multi-item locations, regardless of whether the child containers under that parent have multiple items or not.

 

            
Use the Disposition Code Required Checkbox to indicate that the user needs to scan in a disposition code that the 

system will associate with each item checked in. A disposition code indicates if an item is in good condition, is 

damaged, etc. These are helpful when processing returns.





            
Use the Reason Code Required Checkbox to have the system force the user to enter a reason code when checking in items. 

Note that this setting is only available when the Disposition Code Required checkbox is selected. Reason codes can be 

configured in the Quality History Reason Codes Window (set the process to Receiving).





            
Use the Single Unit Scan Checkbox to  perform a rapid scanning of individual items for receipt check in. When this configuration is set, you can perform a receipt check in of single unit of item without the system displaying the partial check in screen. When a single unit is scanned, then system will  check in for one quantity in the base unit of measurement and then update the receipt header, detail quantity and adjust the inventory at receiving dock locations.  Note: This option will be disabled if any one of the options are selected/active in the receiving preference - Allow over receiving, License plate assignment method is set to 'Manual', Disposition code required, QC inspection selected, Verify item dimension and Verify item unit of measure.





            
Use the QC Inspection Active Checkbox to that you want the system to check every item you check in to see if 

it is eligible for the quality control process.





            
Use the Verify Item Dimensions Checkbox to determine if the system will check item dimensions when checking in items. If 

any item does not have dimension(s), the user can choose whether the check in should continue or not:- If this checkbox 

is selected, the system will display a message warning the user that all the dimensions are not defined. The user then 

will be able to continue or cancel the check in, knowing that all the dimensions are not defined. Choose "Yes" 
 to continue with the check in, or "No" to cancel.- If the checkbox is not selected, the system will not check to see 

if an item has dimensions when performing a check in.





            
Use the Verify 
 Item Unit of Measure Checkbox to determine if the user is required to confirm that a receipt 
 has the same quantity per container as the system expects: 



- If this checkbox is selected, 
 the system will display a verification window each time this user checks 
 in a container. This verification window displays the unit of measure 
 amounts that are defined on the storage template record for the item or 
 item class (or the *Default record). The user can either attest that these 
 values are correct or change them. Any changes made apply only containers 
 on this receipt.



- If this 
 checkbox is not selected, the system will not ask the user to verify the container's quantity. 



Note that this setting also applies when creating pre-check in receipt containers.
 

        

        
 

        
Using the Authorized Users Tab

        

            
The Authorized Users Tab is  used to authorize users for the preference record. A user can be authorized to one to many receiving preferences. On creating a new receiving preference, all users will be automatically authorized to the new preference.  Using the List option, the user authorization can be restricted. Only receiving preferences for the authorized user will be available from the Receipt workbench and RF Receiving screens.
